finding.claim: SSRF in POST /profile/avatar: the only control is a startsWith('https://') check, which does not restrict the destination host. An attacker can make the server fetch https://internal-host, https://169.254.169.254, https://localhost, or any hostname that resolves to a private IP. Axios also follows redirects by default (maxRedirects 5, including https to http), so an attacker-controlled https server can 302 to http://users.internal:8080 or the cloud metadata endpoint. The response body is not returned, only its byte length, so this is partly blind. It still allows internal port and host probing through status, error and length differences, and it can trigger side-effecting GETs.
finding.source: req.body.avatarUrl (JSON body of POST /profile/avatar, unauthenticated; no auth middleware exists)

trace.note: only checks typeof string and startsWith('https://'); no host parsing, no allowlist, no private/loopback/link-local IP block, no DNS resolution check
axios.get(url) with default redirect following and no maxRedirects:0 or beforeRedirect validation
img.data.length returned to the caller, which gives a size oracle

finding.guards_checked: The startsWith('https://') scheme prefix check is enforced (returns 400) but is insufficient: it is not a host allowlist and does not block internal or metadata hosts. No redirect restriction. No IP or DNS validation. No auth on the route. Dispositions: E1 (POST /profile/avatar) to S1 (axios.get at line 14) is VULNERABLE. E2 (GET /users/:id) to S2 (axios.get at line 20) is SAFE for SSRF: the host is the constant USER_SVC, the id is passed through encodeURIComponent so it cannot change the host, port or scheme or inject '/', '?' or '#', and a '..' id could at most traverse the path within the fixed internal service (not reported as SSRF).

verdict.guard_found: Only a typeof string and startsWith('https://') prefix check at server.js:11; no host allowlist, IP/DNS validation, redirect restriction, or auth middleware.
verdict.reason: server.js:10 takes req.body.avatarUrl from an unauthenticated route, server.js:11 only checks the 'https://' prefix (not a closing guard), and server.js:14 passes it to axios.get with default redirect following, so the SSRF (blind, byte length returned at server.js:15) holds.
